text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich's high profile press secretary, Tony Blankley, is leaving after nearly seven years, the speaker said Thursday.

"I knew we were in danger of losing Tony when we were in San Diego (for the Republican convention) and people began coming up to him for his autograph," Gingrich told Reuters, saying Blankley was "honest, intelligent and he does a great job."

Blankley's departure is one of several personnel changes in Gingrich's office. Arne Christenson has moved up to be chief of staff, replacing Dan Meyer, and Communications Coordinator Leigh Ann Metzger is also leaving.
Blankley, the speaker's alter-ego for years, was away from the office and not immediately available.

He will leave at year's end, although his plans are uncertain. He has been rumoured as a potential radio or television talk show host and has lost more than 30 pounts on a diet that cut out cigarettes, alcohol and fatty foods.
